name: Paramānanda Purī

## The well that became the Gaṅgā (Antya 3.232–258)

«The Lord had great affection for Paramānanda Purī, just like that found between the two close friends Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna.» One day, at his monastery, the Lord asked about the water of his well. — «This well is very unfortunate, for its water is always completely muddy.» — «Alas, Jagannātha has become miserly. Anyone who touches the water from Paramānanda Purī's well will be delivered, even if he is most sinful…» Raising His arms, the Lord prayed: «Please order the Bhogavatī Gaṅgā, which flows in Pātāla-loka, to enter this well.» In the morning the well was full of crystal-clear water; Purī Gosvāmī fainted in ecstasy and the devotees circumambulated it. The Lord bathed in it and drank from it, and said:

> «Know for certain that I live in this world simply because of Purī Gosvāmī's affection. I belong to Purī Gosvāmī. There is no doubt about this. If he likes he can even sell Me. Anyone who sees Purī Gosvāmī even once will become qualified to attain love for Kṛṣṇa.» (3.255–257)

## The Lord's two arms (Antya 10.46–49)

«Among the Lord's sannyāsī associates, there was no one as dear to the Lord as Paramānanda Purī. Paramānanda Purī and Svarūpa Dāmodara were the two most qualified devotees among the Lord's sannyāsī associates… Paramānanda Purī was always engaged in meditation, and Śrī Svarūpa was always engaged in chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa mahā-mantra. In this way these two sannyāsīs were like the arms of Lord Caitanya.»
